subject: Error when fitting the same models with gdistsamp mixture "NB"

messages.author: 3ba16c5ec288c557
messages.subject: Error when fitting the same models with gdistsamp mixture "NB"
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to link the abundances of some forest bird species with the structure parameters of forests in Catalonia (Spain). As the abundances data come from a distance sampling method survey, I used the distsamp function to fit the models for each species and the parboot function to check if they were a good fit. Although the results were not good, likely due to overdispersion, it all seemed to work with no warnings or errors. However, I tried fitting the same models with the gdistsamp function, with the numPrimary = 1 in a new unmarkedFrameGDS and the phiformula = 1 too and the negative binomial distribution (mixture = "NB"), following the examples set in the "Applied Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology Vol. 1". For some species, the models were fitted and nothing is wrong. However, for some other species, the function fails and it produces the next error:

Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) :
non-finite finite-difference value [15] Calls: .rs.sourceWithProgress -> eval -> eval -> gdistsamp -> optim

I am not sure if there is an easy solution for that? I tried selecting again the key function running new null models but with the gdistsamp function and checking the AICs, and for some species it changed (e.g. one species with distsamp the null model with "hazard" had a lower AIC than with "halfnorm" but viceversa whith gidstsamp) and specifically for one that changed it now fitted the model when it failed before (with the error posted here). 

I'm relatively new to coding and modeling, especially hierarchical occupancy models, so I apologize in advance if I am too vague. Any extra information needed, I can provide.

Any insights or suggestions on how to address this issue would be greatly appreciated!

Best,
Gabri

messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Error when fitting the same models with gdistsamp mixture "NB"
parts:
Dear Gabri,

 

Sometimes gdistsamp benefits from using lower order numbers. For example, if you are using metres, try dividing distances by 100.

 

We will get back to you!

José

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Error when fitting the same models with gdistsamp mixture "NB"
parts:
Dear José,

thank you very much for the insight! I tried it and it worked for all but one species, so that was an improvement, for sure. However, when using the parboot and crossval functions to check the goodness of fit and cross validation for all fitted models, for some of them are not working and tells me the following error:

Error in integrate(gxhaz, db[j], db[j + 1], shape = shape[i, t], scale = scale,  :  the integral is probably divergent 
Calls: .rs.sourceWithProgress ... fitted -> .local -> getP -> getP -> .local -> integrate

Also, for most that do actually work, a big proportion of simulations are failing (I am doing 100 simulations for each model, and for some its only 1-10 simulations failed, but some 80-99 and even one, all 100 simulations fail). That can be solved by just doing more simulations until for each species I have 100 that did not fail, but for the one that failed all simulations it's a problem. 

Best,
Gabri
